The challenge today
Excel got you started.
It won’t keep you safe.
No single source of truth
Every sheet is a different version. The numbers never quite agree.
Stock is a guess
On-hand quantities are only true the day someone counts them.
Medicine expires on the shelf
No expiry or batch tracking means silent write-offs every month.
Critical items run out
Nothing warns you when insulin or gloves quietly hit zero.
Money you can’t see
Who owes you, how much, how overdue? Buried across tabs.
No accountability
Anyone can change any cell — and no one knows who did.
Every one of these is a real cost — in cash, in spoilage, and in patient trust.

02 · Medical traceability
Never write off expired stock again
Every batch carries its expiry date — and the system sells oldest-first (FEFO) on its own.
Cold-chain items like Insulin live in a dedicated Cold Storage (2–8°C) location.
Full recall traceability — find every unit of a bad lot in seconds.
Lots grouped by location — note Cold Storage (2–8°C)
Lot + expiryFEFO removalCold Storage 2–8°CRecall-ready

03 · Never run out
The system watches your stock so you don’t have to
Set a min / max per item: Insulin 20/80, Paracetamol 50/200, Gloves 30/120.
When stock hits the minimum, it flags — or drafts the purchase order — automatically.
No more learning about a stockout from an unhappy customer.

Buy in USD, sell in SDG — your margin protected automatically
